author: Tehsmash
raw_text:
It might be worth calling out that we send the full Task first to prevent any race conditions, i.e. if we required the client to do GetTask then Resubscribe there is a window where an update could be missed.

Alternatively, we could require a resourceVersion number on the Task object, and something like we have in k8s: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/#efficient-detection-of-changes

author: Tehsmash
raw_text:
Why only for authenticated clients?

We seem to have a chicken and eggs problem in this case:

```
The client MUST authenticate the request using one of the schemes declared in the public `AgentCard.securitySchemes` and `AgentCard.security` fields.
```

How can it the client get the "public" card if this endpoint is only available for authenticated clients?

Today you can start with as little information as a known URL which serves A2A on a known transport, then fetch the AgentCard to decide your next steps like authenticating or change to a more desirable transport etc.

This is probably stepping into a larger discussion about the role of AgentCards and discovery which I would like to be part of.

author: Tehsmash
raw_text: Seems weird that this method isn't grouped with the other task related operations (resubscribe etc), and the AgentCard operation is in-between. Might be worth re-ordering the spec slightly to make that make more sense, or even creating explicit groups of operations on objects, like GetTask, Resubscribe etc are all operations on a Task.

author: Tehsmash
raw_text:
Should we define a standard format for the extensions field? i.e. it should be a comma separated string of extension identifiers. That way, the way the string is transported is transport specific, but the server side parsing of the desired extensions is the same regardless of transport?

Is there a reason (other than backwards compatiblity) to not add this into the main request input models? For example adding an "enabled-extensions" field along side "metadata" in SendMessage, for HTTP/REST this could be translated to a query param which works for GET and POST for example, and for gRPC it would simply be another field in SendMessageRequest.

Actually, it looks like "extensions" is already there so we could change the semantics if provided by the client these are the desired extensions to enable, if they are not supported by the server it can choose to reject the request.

This is similar to how taskID is optional in the message body based on whether the message should be posted to an existing task or not.

author: darrelmiller
raw_text: Tasks can be returned after receiving messages.  Task and Message have a `kind` property that is a discriminator. In gRPC there is a wrapper class that has properties for each type.  We need to reconcile this.  It is on the TSC agenda for tomorrow.  I am planning to propose we move to wrapper classes with properties across all transports because discriminator fields come with all kinds of headaches.
